design: Tier 2 (hazard): a migration on the operator's live :8000 data moves every document in the proposed phase (four on 2026-10-27) back to exploring, with a recorded event each, and removes proposed from the allowed phases. Back up :8000's database (sqlite backup API) before the restart that runs it. Rollback: the downgrade re-allows proposed; the moved documents stay in exploring (re-proposing is the operator's one click). Build note: D extends this slice's Build action, so C lands before D.

lifecycle: exploring -> approved -> archived (no proposed). A document is edited freely while exploring; Check reports readiness at any time without moving it. Approve names the content version the operator loaded. After approval the document changes only through amendments (roadmap slice D). Building is an action on an approved document, possibly repeated.

open_questions.question: Built by Claude Code subagents outside the Hub's flows (operator, 2026-10-27), so delivery is none; tasks are closed as already built against the merged commits once their acceptance drives pass.

problem: Operator, 2026-10-26: 'the spec flow feels kind of weird: the propose is actually just a check and approve jumps straight into the flow if it exists'. Today (hub/hub/api/v1/spec.py propose_document :3047, spec_service.py :1954-1995) propose runs the readiness check and moves the document to proposed, where it is frozen until reopened; the agent cannot keep working on it. Approve (spec.py around :3265) accepts the intent, materialises the tasks and, when delivery is a flow, creates and starts the flow in the same click, so the operator cannot approve the what, look at the plan and decide how and when to build. The exploring journey (spec_journey.py JOURNEYS; the delivery step's text ends 'The document is then ready for the operator to propose') decides the build inside the spec. And nothing asks whether the work is already built, which on 2026-10-23 created 13 tasks for shipped work.

requirements.rationale: Propose froze the document, so every finding meant reopening it; the operator wants the agent to keep implementing changes while they look (2026-10-26).
requirements.statement: The operator can Check a document at any time while it is being written; Check reports exactly the blocking gaps and warnings the agent's own save returns, and never changes the document's phase or stops an agent from saving it.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26: move them back to exploring.
requirements.statement: No document can enter a proposed phase, and every document in it when this ships is moved to exploring with a recorded event naming why.
The operator approves a document directly from exploring when it is ready, or over its gaps with approve-anyway as today.

requirements.rationale: With the document editable while the operator reads, an approval could otherwise accept text nobody read (operator, 2026-10-26: refuse).
requirements.statement: An approval names the content version the operator loaded, and is refused, saying the document changed since it was loaded, when the stored content differs; after reloading it is accepted.
Approving a document creates its tasks and starts nothing: no flow is created or fired and no run begins, whatever the document's delivery says.

An approved document has a Build action that starts building it as its recommended build says (in this slice: create and start the flow its delivery describes, or leave the tasks on the board), and the action can be taken later than approval.

requirements.rationale: Approvals are scarce (operator, 2026-10-08); splitting must not cost an extra click when none is wanted.
requirements.statement: 'Approve and build' approves and starts the build in one operator action, with the same refusal rules as approving alone.

The intake step asks whether the work is already built and records the answer with the commits named; approving a document recorded as already built offers to close its tasks as already built (slice B) instead of laying them out for building.

requirements.rationale: The 2026-10-25 flow paid a tick, a reviewer wait and a gate run per fine-grained task; the integrator who won used coarse units.
requirements.statement: The tasks step's instructions ask for one task per independently demonstrable piece, built by one agent, naming the files it edits and the tasks it waits on, rather than one task per layer or per file.

requirements.rationale: How it is built is now chosen when building starts (slice D); the spec suggests, the operator decides.
requirements.statement: The last exploring step records a recommended build with a reason for each choice, Build and 'Approve and build' open with it filled in, and a project's spec/journey.json that names the old 'delivery' step still works.

No step text, tool description, readiness message or charter the Hub ships tells an agent or the operator to propose a document; the spec author charter's rule about when to ask in the reply and when to call ask_user refers to approval instead of proposal.

in_scope: Check as an operator action that reports readiness without changing phase
Retiring the proposed phase, with documents now proposed moved back to exploring

Approval laying out tasks with nothing started; Build as a separate action; 'Approve and build' as one action
Intake asking whether the work is already built, and approval then offering close-as-built (slice B's action)
The tasks step asking for coarse tasks; the last step recommending a build with reasons; 'delivery' kept as an alias in spec/journey.json
Step texts, tool descriptions, readiness messages and the spec author charter no longer speaking of proposing
The current spec page header's buttons (Check, Approve, Build, Approve and build), until the redesigned page (slice F) replaces it
non_goals: Build drivers, levels, people, budgets and amendments: roadmap slice D. In this slice a build is what delivery does today (a flow, or tasks left on the board)
The redesigned spec page: slice F, which wires its approved mock to what this slice provides
Roadmap documents' own lifecycle beyond losing the proposed phase

summary: The spec flow stops mixing decisions. Check replaces Propose: it shows the readiness the agent already sees and never changes the phase, so the agent keeps editing while the operator looks. The proposed phase is retired. Approving accepts the version the operator loaded (refused if it changed since), and lays the tasks out as a plan with nothing running. Building is a separate action, with an 'Approve and build' shortcut. The exploring steps follow: intake asks whether the work is already built, the tasks step asks for coarse tasks, the last step recommends a build with reasons instead of deciding one, and nothing the Hub ships still tells anyone to propose.

tasks.description: Remove the proposed phase from the lifecycle and the routes that reach it, migrate proposed documents to exploring with an event, let approve go from exploring, make approval carry the loaded content version and refuse a mismatch; Check as an operator route that returns readiness and moves nothing.
